title: XY16 gallery near decoder fails with a split indirect Y index
summary: Fixed locally in 0002: fused near byte/word Y accesses preserve the full index across allocation and REP/SEP insertion. A distinct near-address bank-wrap defect also contributed to the gallery failure and is repaired by an unsigned-wrap proof in address folding. The unchanged 62-work benchmark fails on the reconstructed baseline and fusion-only build, then passes with both repairs (0x5CF0).

resolution.change: Fused LD/STIndirYIdx{,16}Fused pseudos in 0002, plus the separately recorded MOSLegalizerInfo near-index bank-wrap guard.
resolution.causal_explanation: LDYImag16 and the indirect access were separate instructions, allowing X8 spill reloads to insert SEP #$10 and destroy Y.high. A four-byte pseudo consumes the Imag16 index, defines all of Y16, preserves memory operands and expands after width insertion to adjacent LDY/access. Fusion alone repairs the reduced byte decoder with and without LTO. The original gallery also requires the distinct modulo-16-bit address repair in mos-near-index-bank-wrap; bank-$00 RAM mirrors hid that second failure in the reduced decoder.
resolution.trigger_check: Preserved reduced-decoder MIR shows LDYImag16, SEP #16, X8 spill reloads and LDIndirYIdx. Selected-MIR tests require a full Y16 definition for byte/word load/store fusion and retained volatile MMOs. Original LTO gallery bitcode and stage WRAM establish that fusion alone leaves near backreferences reading DBR+1. The identical original gallery source passes only after both changes.
